summary.headline: Endurance Q1 FY27 standalone total income rose 35.9% to ₹3,194.15 crores, with EBITDA margin at 11.2% after a commodity pass-through headwind.
summary.overview: Standalone total income grew 35.9% YoY to ₹3,194.15 crores, EBITDA rose 17.1% to ₹357.78 crores (11.2% margin) and PAT rose 17.4% to ₹194.62 crores. Management said commodity inflation (RMC at 68.4% of total income vs 64.8% a year ago) compressed margins; ex this pass-through, EBITDA margin would be 13.33%. Consolidated PAT grew 8% to ₹244.52 crores, with Maxwell turning PAT-positive for the first time. Management expects Q2 and Q3 margins to improve as raw material and conversion cost increases are settled with OEMs, and cited multiple SOPs and order wins across 2W, 4W castings, batteries and non-auto solar products.

segments.name: India auto (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q1 India order wins were ₹391.6 crores (₹365.4 crores replacement, ₹26.1 crores new), with ₹373 crores from 2W and ₹18.6 crores from 4W; ₹336 crores came from HMSI, including ₹219.6 crores of suspension facelift business at better margins.

segments.name: Europe (Stöferle/Endurance Overseas)
segments.commentary: Booked €13.9 million of orders in Q1, including a Mercedes hybrid transmission component (100% volume after a competitor's bankruptcy, SOP January 2027) and a Stellantis ICE program. Q1 EBITDA margin 18.2%.

segments.name: Maxwell (BMS/electronics)
segments.commentary: Total income ₹56.5 crores; ₹13 crores of new orders in Q1 took cumulative orders to ₹238 crores per annum (peak in Q2 FY28); RFQ pipeline above ₹300 crores.

segments.name: Aluminium castings (4W)
segments.commentary: 4W casting business about ₹180 crores in Q1 with 6% 4W share; AURIC Shendra cumulative bookings reached ₹513 crores per annum, SOP from September 2026; Hyundai/Kia order of ₹80 crores per annum started this month.

segments.name: Non-auto solar products
segments.commentary: Solar damper and actuator business won totals ₹345 crores (₹118 crores dampers, ₹227 crores actuators); Spanish client SOP started in August 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management expects all raw material increases to be recovered from OEMs in Q2, with aluminium alloy rates softening by ₹12-17/kg; Q2 and Q3 margins expected to be better than Q1, though no quantum given.
Gas, fuel and manpower increases expected to be settled with OEMs in Q2 or Q3.
India capex in FY27 expected similar to FY26 level of about ₹800 crores (FY26 vs ₹611 crores in FY25); mgmt said capex including Tier-2 vendors would be higher.
Brake capacity target of 9 million disc brake assemblies and 9.6 million brake discs per annum by Q1 FY28; ABS capacity addition reduced to 9 lakh units from 12 lakh.
Alloy wheel plants expected to be at full capacity by end FY27; Maxwell orders to peak in Q2 FY28; full impact of Stöferle integration expected from September 2027.
Maharashtra incentive raised to ₹858 crores from ₹600 crores, availed through state GST refund over about seven years.
capex_capacity: Chennai disc brake plant: phase one machinery shifting from Waluj; phase two due Q3 FY27; capacity 3 million disc brake assemblies and 4 million discs per annum; Royal Enfield SOP expected next month.

ABS capacity planned at 9 lakh units per annum added to existing 6.4 lakh; SOP for ABS and CBS hydraulic brake expansion expected September or early October 2026; Bajaj dual channel ABS 120,000 units SOP this quarter, second programme of 120,000 units in Q3 FY27.
Alloy wheels: Chakan about 3 million sets (fully used) and Bidkin 1.8 million sets (about 60% utilised); total 4.8 million wheel sets.

Suspension: monthly capacity to reach 100,000 inverted front forks and shocks by end FY27; Pantnagar SOP of 25,000 sets per month from Q4 FY27; Hero and Suzuki SOP in Q3 FY27 (about ₹120 crores per annum).

Battery packs: Mindewadi assembly line capacity of about 17,000-18,000 packs per month expected to be fully used by October 2026; 4W battery pack capex of ₹62 crores with SOP by Q4 FY27; new SMT line for ECUs and BMS starts next month; fifth aluminium forging press SOP next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jhawar (Investec): How many Europe order intake quality and product mix, given ~€14 million in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Venuti said the Mercedes hybrid transmission component was won because Endurance already had the part; a competitor holding 40% volume went bankrupt, so 100% moves to Endurance with SOP January 2027, and the competitor stops production at year end.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jhawar: Progress on Stöferle integration and timing of benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Managerial and commercial integration 100% complete; sourcing raw castings externally, with an agreement for higher casting capacity targeted by January 2027; full impact expected from September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Arvind Sharma (Citi): Europe revenue, EBITDA, PAT and demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnover €104.3 million (+1.1%), EBITDA €18.9 million (18.2% vs 17.4%), net €4.4 million (vs €6.4 million) as depreciation rose to €11.6 million from €8.5 million; cash profit €16 million (+7.9%). Venuti said no major volume reduction seen yet, with OEM restructuring reports and dealer-stock run-down noted.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jhawar: Can the Q1 commodity headwind recovery and Q2 inflation be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Jain said all raw material increases should be recovered from OEMs in Q2 (Q1 base rates), aluminium alloy rates softening ₹12-17/kg, and conversion cost recovery partly in Q2 and partly Q3; Q2 and Q3 margins better than Q1 but no quantum given.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jhawar: 4W die-casting journey, Shendra progress and OEM engagement?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹180 crores 4W business in Q1 (6% 4W share, mostly castings); Shendra ₹513 crores per annum bookings with SOP September 2026 and peak in early FY29; Hyundai/Kia ₹80 crores per annum started this month; focus shifting to 4W and non-auto castings over 2W.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jhawar: 2W battery pack margin profile and use of in-house BMS?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin number yet; pricing started, BOM work ongoing, guidance deferred to next call. Assembly line capacity of 17,000-18,000 packs per month to be fully used by October; BMS and casting are in-house for existing 2W order; 4W battery pack targeted by Q4 FY27 with a similar margin target to the company average.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi Gupta (InCred): Why is capex guidance flat when key customers are raising capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Jain said capacity already exists; FY27 India capex to be similar to ~₹800 crores in FY26, with Tier-2 vendor capex on top; capex to rise if large opportunities arrive; standalone growth ex raw material content still ~23.5-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi Gupta: Does scooterisation reduce 2W TAM; and why is European order book declining?
qa_highlights.answer: Scooter share has risen from under 10% to 14.3%; scooters grew ~32.7%. For Europe, Jain attributed softer order intake to Chinese OEMs importing powertrains and Korean brands; M&A cited as a growth route, with more clarity promised at next investor call.

qa_highlights.question: Nishit Jalan (Axis): Current 2W market shares and EV-specific product plans; alloy wheel utilisation and the battery pack ownership?
qa_highlights.answer: Brake 34.5%, front forks 44%, shock absorbers 37%; alloy wheels 4.8 million sets total with Chakan 3 million fully used and Bidkin 1.8 million at 60%, full by end FY27; clutch assemblies 3.5% of India sales, rest EV-relevant; battery packs sit in standalone (Mindewadi), not Maxwell.

demand_pricing: India order wins Q1 FY27 ₹391.6 crores (₹365.4 crores replacement, ₹26.1 crores new); ICE ₹380.3 crores, EV ₹11.3 crores; 2W ~₹373 crores, 4W ₹18.6 crores; HMSI ₹336 crores including ₹219.6 crores suspension facelift at better margins.
Total RFQs in hand ₹4,526 crores; cumulative India EV-related wins ₹1,496 crores ex Bajaj (₹1,806 crores incl. Bajaj); orders since FY23 ₹5,270 crores (₹4,241 crores new), excluding Maxwell.

Europe: order intake €13.9 million in Q1 including Mercedes hybrid transmission component (100% volume after competitor bankruptcy, SOP January 2027) and Stellantis ICE programme; Europe turnover €104.3 million (+1.1%), EBITDA €18.9 million (18.2%), net result €4.4 million (down 31% on higher depreciation of €11.6 million).

Pricing and margin: RMC rose to 68.4% of total income vs 64.8%; commodity increases above ₹300 crores paid upfront in Q1 with quarter lag; management says aluminium alloy rates softening ₹12-17/kg, which are about 60% of Q1 raw material purchases; standalone EBITDA margin ex pass-through 13.33%.

Competition and market: Europe EU new car sales +7.4% in Q1 with BEV share 21.9%; Chinese OEMs (BYD +167%, Chery +272%, Leapmotor +500%) driving registrations while production fell 5%; India 2W sales +23.6%, share in scooters 14.3% and brake/fork/shock shares 34.5%/44%/37%.
risks_watch: Q2 and Q3 margin recovery depends on OEM settlements of steel, rubber, plastics, gas, fuel, manpower and conversion cost increases; no quantum given.
Europe: order book softness attributed to Chinese OEM and Korean imports; OEM restructuring reports at Mercedes and Volkswagen; depreciation rising as ICE assets run off over ~18 months.
ABS capacity cut to 9 lakh units from 12 lakh to free machinery for brake assembly; ABS and CBS SOP timing (Sept/early Oct 2026) hinges on final government guidelines not yet issued.
New battery pack and Maxwell ramps (Mindewadi, Bidkin, Maxwell peak Q2 FY28) with margins not yet disclosed for battery packs; ramp-up timing risks.
Capex flat at ~₹800 crores despite peer capex increases; management said it could rise if large opportunities arrive.
Shendra castings peak not until early FY29, and certification lead times for foreign OEMs may delay the revenue ramp.

We are not losing but at the same time with this high growth like I mentioned last quarter, scooters has grown around 32.7%, but still our share is 14.3%.
There's no gap because we already have the capacities.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India demand, order wins and near-term margin recovery, but cautious and non-committal on Q2 margin quantum, Europe order momentum and battery-pack margins, which management deferred to the next call.

growth.why: Standalone total income grew 35.9% YoY in Q1 and India order wins of ₹391.6 crores plus multiple SOPs in Q2–Q3 support growth, but no revenue guidance is given, margins are compressed by commodity pass-through, and the company's own utilisation is only 60% at Bidkin alloy wheels.
